title.zh: 卷四十 列傳第三十四 司馬褧 到漑 劉顯 劉之遴 弟之享 許懋
title.en: Volume 40: Sima Jiong; Dao Gai; Liu Xian; Liu Zhilin; Liu Zhixian; Xu Mao
title.raw: 卷四十 列傳第三十四 司馬褧 到漑 劉顯 劉之遴 弟之享 許懋 Volume 40: Sima Jiong; Dao Gai; Liu Xian; Liu Zhilin; Liu Zhixian; Xu Mao

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第四十 列傳第三十四

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34

sentences.zh: 司馬褧 到漑 劉顯 劉之遴 弟之享 許懋

translations.literal: Sima Jiong; Dao Gai; Liu Xian; Liu Zhilin; his brother Zhixian; Xu Mao
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong; Dao Gai; Liu Xian; Liu Zhilin; his brother Zhixian; Xu Mao

sentences.zh: 司馬褧字元素，河內溫人也。

translations.literal: Sima Jiong, courtesy name Yuansu, was a native of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, styled Yuansu, came from Wen in Henei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖純之，晉大司農高密敬王。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chunzhi was Jin Minister of Finance and Prince Jing of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chunzhi had been Jin’s Minister of Finance and Prince Jing of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 祖讓之，員外常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rangzhi was an External Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rangzhi served as External Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父燮，善《三禮》，仕齊官至國子博士。

translations.literal: His father Xie was expert in the Three Rites; serving Qi, he reached the post of Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie mastered the Three Rites and, under Qi, rose to Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 褧少傳家業，強力專精，手不釋卷，其禮文所涉書，略皆遍睹。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth inherited the family craft, applied himself with fierce concentration, and never laid his scrolls aside; of every ritual text his work touched, he had looked into nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Jiong carried on the family learning, drove himself without relent, and scarcely set a book down; among ritual writings, there was scarcely one he had not read through.

sentences.zh: 沛國劉曁獻爲儒者宗，嘉其學，深相賞好。

translations.literal: Liu Yun of Pei, acclaimed as patriarch of the ru, honored his learning and was deeply fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun of Pei, hailed as doyen of the Confucian scholars, admired his erudition and became his warm friend.

sentences.zh: 少與樂安任昉善，昉亦推重焉。

translations.literal: In youth he was close with Ren Fang of Le’an, who likewise held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was intimate with Ren Fang of Le’an, who also prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 初爲國子生，起家奉朝請，稍遷王府行參軍。

translations.literal: He first served as a student of the National University, entered office as Supporter of the Court, and was soon promoted to Administrative Officer on the prince’s staff.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a National University student, took his first post as Supporter of the Court, and soon became an administrative officer on a princely staff.

sentences.zh: 天監初，詔通儒治五禮，有司舉褧治嘉禮，除尚書祠部郎中。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tianjian, an edict called on broad scholars to compile the Five Rites; the authorities nominated Jiong to work on the ceremonial rites, and he was appointed Attendant Gentleman in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjian opened, the throne ordered learned men to shape the Five Rites; Jiong was put forward for the ceremonial canon and made Attendant Gentleman in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 是時創定禮樂，褧所議多見施行。

translations.literal: At that time ritual and music were being newly fixed, and many of Jiong’s proposals were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was founding its ritual music, much of what Jiong proposed was adopted.

sentences.zh: 除步兵校尉，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and concurrently Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commandant of Footsoldiers and also Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 褧學尤精於事數，國家吉凶禮，當世名儒明山賓、賀蒨等疑不能斷，皆取決焉。

translations.literal: Jiong’s learning was especially sharp in liturgical minutiae; for state rites of fortune and calamity, celebrated ru of the day—Mingshan Bin, He Qian, and others—when they could not decide, all turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong excelled above all in the arithmetic of ceremony; when eminent ritualists such as Mingshan Bin and He Qian could not settle a point of state rite, they took his word as final.

sentences.zh: 累遷正員郎、鎮南諮議參軍，兼舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Regular Attendant and Military Advisor to the Defender of the South, still holding his post as Master of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Regular Attendant and military advisor to the Defender of the South, keeping his palace secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 出爲仁威長史、長沙內史。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to Renwei and Interior Magistrate of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as chief clerk to Renwei and magistrate of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 還除雲騎將軍，兼御史中丞，頃之卽真。

translations.literal: On return he was made General of Clouded Cavalry and acting Censor-in-Chief; before long the acting title became permanent.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became General of Clouded Cavalry and acting Censor-in-Chief; soon the acting post was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出爲宣毅南康王長史、行府國並石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: In year sixteen he went out as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Nankang, Xuanyi, with charge of the princely administration and the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he served as chief clerk to Prince Xuanyi of Nankang, directing both the princely household and the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 褧雖居外官，有敕預文德、武德二殿長名問訊，不限日。

translations.literal: Though serving outside the capital, he received orders to attend the Wende and Wude Halls for roster salutation with no fixed schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Even while posted abroad, he was ordered to present himself for roster greeting at the Wende and Wude halls whenever summoned.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷明威將軍、晉安王長史，未幾卒。

translations.literal: In year seventeen he was transferred to General of Illustrious Might and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Jin’an; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Year seventeen brought him the rank of General of Illustrious Might and chief clerk to the Prince of Jin’an; he died not long after.

sentences.zh: 王命記室庾肩吾集其文爲十卷，所撰《嘉禮儀注》一百一十二卷。

translations.literal: The prince ordered Recorder Yu Jianyi to collect his writings in ten scrolls; he also authored Ceremonial Rites with Commentary in one hundred twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had Yu Jianyi compile his writings in ten scrolls; Jiong himself had composed Ceremonial Rites with Commentary in one hundred twelve scrolls.

sentences.zh: 到漑字茂灌，彭城武原人。

translations.literal: Dao Gai, courtesy name Maoguan, was a native of Wuyuan in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Gai, styled Maoguan, came from Wuyuan in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 曾祖彥之，宋驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yanzhi was a Cavalry General of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yanzhi had been Song’s Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 祖仲度，驃騎江夏王從事中郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhongdu was Attendant on the King of Jiangxia, Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhongdu served the King of Jiangxia, Cavalry General, as attendant.

sentences.zh: 父坦，齊中書郎。

translations.literal: His father Tan was a Secretariat Gentleman of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan was a Secretariat Gentleman under Qi.

sentences.zh: 漑少孤貧，與弟洽俱聰敏有才學，早爲任昉所知，由是聲名益廣。

translations.literal: Gai was orphaned young and poor; he and his younger brother Qia were both clever and talented, early known to Ren Fang, and his reputation spread all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Gai lost his parents early and grew up poor; he and his brother Qia were both bright and learned, noticed early by Ren Fang, and his name rang farther still.

sentences.zh: 起家王國左常侍，轉後軍法曹行參軍，歷殿中郎。

translations.literal: He entered office as Left Regular Attendant in the prince’s domain, became Acting Administrative Officer of the Rear Army, and served through as a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as left regular attendant in a princely fief, became acting administrative officer of the Rear Army, and rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲建安內史，遷中書郎，兼吏部，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He went out as Interior Magistrate of Jian’an, was promoted Secretariat Gentleman, jointly held the Ministry of Personnel, and Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Jian’an, then became Secretariat Gentleman, joint director of the Ministry of Personnel, and attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹爲會稽太守，以漑爲輕車長史、行府郡事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, was Governor of Kuaiji, Gai was made Chief Clerk of Light Chariots with charge of the prefecture and princely administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yi of Xiangdong governed Kuaiji, Gai was made chief clerk of light chariots with full charge of prefecture and princely affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖敕王曰：「到漑非直爲汝行事，足爲汝師，間有進止，每須詢訪。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor instructed the prince: “Dao Gai is not merely here to work for you; he is fit to be your teacher. Whenever anything arises, you must consult him.”
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor told the prince, “Dao Gai is not simply your agent—he is fit to be your teacher. On every matter you should seek his counsel.”

sentences.zh: 」遭母憂，居喪盡禮，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he observed mourning to the letter, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother’s death he mourned to the last propriety, and the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，猶蔬食布衣者累載。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, he ate only vegetables and wore plain cloth for years.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was done, he kept to vegetables and plain cloth for years on end.

sentences.zh: 除通直散騎常侍，御史中丞，太府卿，都官尚書，郢州長史、江夏太守，加招遠將軍，入爲左民尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary with Unimpeded Access, Censor-in-Chief, Director of the Palace Treasuries, Minister Director of Justice, Chief Clerk and Governor of Jiangxia in Yingzhou, with promotion to General Who Attracts from Afar, then entered court as Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: He became Regular Attendant with unimpeded access, Censor-in-Chief, Director of the Palace Treasuries, Minister Director of Justice, chief clerk and governor of Jiangxia in Yingzhou, then General Who Attracts from Afar, and finally returned as Minister of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 漑身長八尺，美風儀，善容止，所蒞以清白自脩。

translations.literal: Gai stood eight feet tall, with handsome bearing and graceful deportment; wherever he served he cultivated himself in integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet in stature, with striking presence and measured grace, he kept his conduct white wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 性又率儉，不好聲色，虛室單床，傍無姬侍。

translations.literal: By nature he was also plain and frugal, indifferent to music and women; his rooms held only a bare bed and no concubine attended him.
translations.idiomatic: He was spare by temperament, caring nothing for music or women; his chamber held a single bed and no attendant concubine.

sentences.zh: 自外車服，不事鮮華，冠履十年一易，朝服或至穿補，傳呼清路，示有朝章而已。

translations.literal: Beyond that, he cared nothing for show in carriage or dress; cap and shoes he changed once in ten years, court robes sometimes worn to holes, yet when heralds cleared the road it was only to observe what office required.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage and garments he kept unadorned; cap and shoes he replaced once a decade, court robes sometimes patched through, yet when runners cleared the way it was only to honor the dignity of office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，坐事左遷金紫光祿大夫，俄授散騎常侍、侍中、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted for an offense to Grand Master for the Imperial Clan with the Golden Ornament; soon after he was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Chamberlain for Attendants, and Grand Master of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was demoted to Grand Master for the Imperial Clan with the Golden Ornament for an offense; soon he was again Regular Attendant, Chamberlain for Attendants, and Grand Master of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 漑素謹厚，特被高祖賞接，每與對棊，從夕達旦。

translations.literal: Gai was by nature cautious and steadfast and enjoyed special favor from the Founding Emperor; they often played go from evening till dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and decorous, he won unusual favor from the Founding Emperor, who would play go with him from dusk until daybreak.

sentences.zh: 漑第山池有奇石，高祖戲與賭之，幷《禮記》一部，漑並輸焉，未進，高祖謂朱异曰；

translations.literal: In Gai’s residence among hills and pools was a strange stone; the emperor jested of wagering for it along with a full copy of the Book of Rites, and Gai lost both—but had not yet delivered them when the emperor said to Zhu Yi:
translations.idiomatic: Among the hills and pools at Gai’s house stood a curious stone; the emperor wagered it against a complete Book of Rites, and Gai lost both—yet before he could send them over, the emperor said to Zhu Yi:

sentences.zh: 「卿謂到漑所輸可以送未？

translations.literal: “Do you think what Dao Gai has lost can be sent yet?”
translations.idiomatic: “Do you suppose Dao Gai’s losses are ready to be delivered?”

sentences.zh: 」漑斂板對曰：「臣旣事君，安敢失禮。

translations.literal: Gai folded his tablet and replied: “Having taken service under my lord, how dare I fail in propriety.”
translations.idiomatic: Gai folded his memorial tablet and answered, “Having become your servant, how dare I be remiss in ritual?”

sentences.zh: 」高祖大笑，其見親愛如此。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed loud; such was his cherished intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily—such was the warmth between them.

sentences.zh: 後因疾失明，詔以金紫光祿大夫、散騎常侍，就第養疾。

translations.literal: Later blindness overtook him through illness; an edict let him hold his posts as Grand Master for the Imperial Clan and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary while convalescing at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later illness took his sight; he was ordered to keep his titles as Grand Master for the Imperial Clan and Regular Attendant while nursing himself at home.

sentences.zh: 漑家門雍睦，兄弟特相友愛。

translations.literal: The Dao household was harmonious; the brothers were deeply fond of one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Dao family lived in concord; the brothers loved one another with uncommon devotion.

sentences.zh: 初與弟洽常共居一齋，洽卒後，便舍爲寺，因斷腥膻，終身蔬食，別營小室，朝夕從僧徒禮誦。

translations.literal: Early on he and his brother Qia had shared one study; after Qia’s death he turned the room into a temple, forsook meat for life, ate only vegetables, and built a small chamber where morning and evening he chanted with the monks.
translations.idiomatic: Once he and Qia had shared a single study; when Qia died he made it a temple, renounced flesh for life, ate only vegetables, and built a small room where dawn and dusk he joined the monks in chant.

sentences.zh: 高祖每月三致淨饌，恩禮甚篤。

translations.literal: Every month on the third day the Founding Emperor sent pure food; his favor was deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: On the third of each month the Founding Emperor sent him pure fare—his kindness ran that deep.

sentences.zh: 蔣山有延賢寺者，漑家世創立，故生平公俸，咸以供焉，略無所取。

translations.literal: On Mount Jiang was Yanxian Monastery, which the Dao family had founded in generations past; his public salary in life all went to it—he took almost nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Jiang stood Yanxian Monastery, founded by the Dao line; in life he poured his official salary into it and kept almost nothing.

sentences.zh: 性又不好交遊，惟與朱异、劉之遴、張綰同志友密。

translations.literal: He also shunned socializing, sharing only close friendship with Zhu Yi, Liu Zhilin, and Zhang Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for society, counting only Zhu Yi, Liu Zhilin, and Zhang Chuan as intimate friends.

sentences.zh: 及臥疾家園，門可羅雀，三君每歲時常鳴騶枉道，以相存問，置酒敘生平，極歡而去。

translations.literal: When sick at home his gate could have been strung with nets for birds; the three friends each year would ride with state escort out of their way to call on him, set wine, recall their lives together, and leave in highest spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Ill at home, his gate might have been hung with nets for sparrows; yet each year the three would ride with official escort out of their way, bring wine, talk over old times, and part in full joy.

sentences.zh: 臨終，托張、劉勒子孫以薄葬之禮，卒時年七十二。

translations.literal: At the end he entrusted Zhang and Liu to urge his sons toward simple burial; he died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he asked Zhang and Liu to press his sons toward a plain funeral; he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈本官。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his last office posthumously.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings in twenty scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, twenty scrolls, circulated abroad.

sentences.zh: 時以漑、洽兄弟比之二陸，故世祖贈詩曰：「魏世重雙丁，晉朝稱二陸，何如今兩到，復似淩寒竹。」

translations.literal: Of the day Gai and Qia were likened to the two Lu brothers, so Emperor Shizong wrote in verse: “Wei prized the twin Dings, Jin acclaimed the two Lus—how does it compare with two Daos now, bamboo braving the cold?”
translations.idiomatic: Men compared Gai and Qia to the two Lu brothers, and Emperor Shizong wrote, “Wei honored the twin Dings, Jin praised the two Lus—what of two Daos today, bamboo standing through the cold?”

sentences.zh: 子鏡，字圓照，安西湘東王法曹行參軍，太子舍人，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Jing, courtesy name Yuanzhao, was Acting Administrative Officer in the Law Bureau of the Prince of Xiangdong in the West, Attendant to the Heir Apparent—and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, styled Yuanzhao, served as acting law officer to the Prince of Western Xiangdong and attendant to the heir apparent, and died young.

sentences.zh: 鏡子藎，早聰慧，起家著作佐郎，歷太子舍人，宣城王主簿，太子洗馬，尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Jing’s son Shen was clever from childhood; he entered office as Assistant Editor in the Palace Library, served as Attendant to the Heir Apparent, secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and Attendant in the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing’s son Shen was precocious; he began in the Palace Library, became attendant to the heir apparent, secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng, groom of the heir apparent, and chancellery attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗從高祖幸京口，登北顧樓賦詩，藎受詔便就，上覽以示漑曰：「藎定是才子，翻恐卿從來文章假手於藎。

translations.literal: Once when he followed the Founding Emperor to Jingkou and the emperor composed a poem on the Northern Prospect Tower, Shen received the command to compose on the spot; the emperor showed it to Gai: “Shen must be a gifted man—I fear your writings all along were Shen’s hand at work.”
translations.idiomatic: Once, when the Founding Emperor visited Jingkou and improvised a poem on the Northern Prospect Tower, Shen was told to answer on the spot; the emperor showed Gai the result: “Shen is surely a talent—I suspect your essays have been his work all along.”

sentences.zh: 」因賜漑《連珠》曰：「研磨墨以騰文，筆飛毫以書信。

translations.literal: He then bestowed on Gai a Linked Pearls verse: “Grind ink for soaring words, let the brush’s tip fly in faithful script.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Gai a Linked Pearls poem: “Grind ink till the words take flight; let the brush-tip race in loyal script.

sentences.zh: 如飛蛾之赴火，豈焚身之可吝。

translations.literal: Like the moth that seeks the flame—how can it spare its body being burned?”
translations.idiomatic: Like the moth that flies to flame—what body would it not burn?”

sentences.zh: 必耄年其已及，可假之於少藎。

translations.literal: When old age must come, one may borrow from young Shen.”
translations.idiomatic: When old age arrives, one may borrow from young Shen.”

sentences.zh: 」其見知賞如此。

translations.literal: Such was the measure of his regard.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his esteem.

sentences.zh: 除丹陽尹丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made assistant magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 太清亂，赴江陵卒。

translations.literal: In the chaos of Taiqing he went to Jiangling and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiqing turmoil he went to Jiangling and died there.

sentences.zh: 劉顯字嗣芳，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xian, courtesy name Sifang, was a native of Xiang in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian, styled Sifang, came from Xiang in Pei.

sentences.zh: 父鬷，晉安內史。

translations.literal: His father Kan was Interior Magistrate of Jin’an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan had been interior magistrate of Jin’an.

sentences.zh: 顯幼而聰敏，當世號曰神童。

translations.literal: Xian was clever from childhood; his contemporaries called him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was bright from childhood; men of his day called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 天監初，舉秀才，解褐中軍臨川王行參軍，俄署法曹。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tianjian he was recommended as a cultivated talent, relieved his clerk’s collar as Administrative Officer on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon served as Chief of the Law Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjian opened he was presented as a cultivated talent, entered service as staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon headed the law bureau.

sentences.zh: 顯好學，博涉多參通，任昉嘗得一篇缺簡書，文字零落，歷示諸人，莫能識者，顯云是《古文尚書》所刪逸篇，昉檢《周書》，果如其說，昉因大相賞異。

translations.literal: Xian loved learning and ranged widely in many fields; once Ren Fang obtained a fragmentary bamboo text with characters scattered and eroded, showed it to everyone, and none could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage deleted from the Old Text Documents, and when Fang checked the Documents of Zhou it matched exactly; Fang was thereafter greatly struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian loved study and ranged across many disciplines; once Ren Fang had a bamboo slip with characters broken and faded, showed it around, and no one could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage cut from the Old Text Documents; Fang checked the Documents of Zhou and found it exact, and from then held him in wonder.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，尚書令沈約命駕造焉，於坐策顯經史十事，顯對其九。

translations.literal: When his mother’s mourning ended, the Minister and Chief Minister of Works Shen Yue came in his carriage to visit, and at the seat tested Xian on ten matters from the classics and histories—Xian answered nine.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother’s mourning, Minister Shen Yue came by carriage to call on him and, seated, examined him on ten points of canon and history—Xian answered nine.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「老夫昏忘，不可受策；

translations.literal: Yue said: “This old man is muddled and forgetful; I cannot submit to examination—”
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, “This old man is dim and forgetful; I cannot sit for your test—”

sentences.zh: 雖然，聊試數事，不可至十也。

translations.literal: “Even so, let me try a few things—you must not reach ten.”
translations.idiomatic: “Still, try me on a few—you must not make it ten.”

sentences.zh: 」顯問其五，約對其二。

translations.literal: Xian questioned him on five; Yue answered two.
translations.idiomatic: Xian put five questions to him; Yue answered two.

sentences.zh: 陸倕聞之歎曰：「劉郎可謂差人，雖吾家平原詣張壯武，王粲謁伯喈，必無此對。

translations.literal: Lu Zuo heard of it and sighed: “One may say Master Liu is a man apart—even when our house’s Lu Ji called on Zhang Hua, or when Wang Can visited Cai Yong, there could not have been such parry and riposte.”
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zuo heard and sighed, “Master Liu is a man apart—even when our Lu Ji sought out Zhang Hua, or Wang Can called on Cai Yong, there was never such an exchange.”

sentences.zh: 」其爲名流推賞如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which leading minds held him.
translations.idiomatic: So the leading men of the age honored him.

sentences.zh: 及約爲太子少傅，乃引爲五官掾，俄兼廷尉正。

translations.literal: When Yue became Mentor to the Heir Apparent, he brought Xian in as Aide in the Five Offices, and soon he also served as Director under the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue became mentor to the heir apparent, he drew Xian in as aide in the Five Offices; soon Xian also served as director under the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 五兵尚書傅昭掌著作，撰國史，引顯爲佐。

translations.literal: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and in charge of historiography, was compiling the national history and brought Xian in as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and overseer of historiography, was compiling the national history and took Xian as his assistant.

sentences.zh: 九年，始革尚書五都選，顯以本官兼吏部郎，又除司空臨川王外兵參軍，遷尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: In year nine the Ministry system was first reformed for the five directorates of selection; Xian in his existing post also served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was further appointed External Military Officer to the Prince of Linchuan, Minister of Ceremonies, and was transferred to Attendant Gentleman for Ceremonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine the five selection directorates were first reformed; Xian kept his post while also serving as director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made external military officer to the Prince of Linchuan, Minister of Ceremonies, and then Attendant Gentleman for Ceremonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗爲《上朝詩》，沈約見而美之，時約郊居宅新成，因命工書人題之於壁。

translations.literal: Once he composed a poem on morning audience; Shen Yue read it with admiration, and at the time Yue’s suburban residence was newly built—he had a scribe paint it on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a poem on the morning audience; Shen Yue admired it, and when Yue’s suburban house was newly finished he had a scribe brush it on the wall.

sentences.zh: 出爲臨川王記室參軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as recorder to the Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 建康平，復入爲尚書儀曹侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he returned as Vice Director of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites and concurrently Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiankang was pacified he returned as vice director of ceremonial affairs and again Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出爲秣陵令，又除驃騎鄱陽王記室，兼中書舍人，累遷步兵校尉、中書侍郎，舍人如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Moling, was again made Recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, with concurrent service as Master of Documents, and was promoted in succession to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Gentleman of the Secretariat, still Master of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Moling, then recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, again Master of Documents, and rose to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Secretariat gentleman, keeping the palace post throughout.

sentences.zh: 顯與河東裴子野、南陽劉之遴、吳郡顧協，連職禁中，遞相師友，時人莫不慕之。

translations.literal: Xian, Pei Ziye of Hedong, Liu Zhilin of Nanyang, and Gu Xie of Wu commandery served together inside the palace in rotation, teaching one another as teacher and friend—the men of the time all envied them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, Pei Ziye of Hedong, Liu Zhilin of Nanyang, and Gu Xie of Wu served together within the palace gates, learning from one another as teacher and friend—men of the age envied them.

sentences.zh: 顯博聞強記，過於裴、顧，時魏人獻古器，有隱起字，無能識者，顯案文讀之，無有滯礙，考校年月，一字不差，高祖甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: Xian’s learning and memory exceeded Pei and Gu; when Wei presented an ancient vessel with raised characters none could read, Xian traced the text without hesitation, checked dates without a single error, and the Founding Emperor was much pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xian’s erudition and memory surpassed Pei and Gu; when Wei sent an antique with raised script no one could decipher, Xian read it straight through, fixed the dates without one mistake, and the Founding Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，除國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and appointed Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣遠岳陽王長史，行府國事，未拜，遷雲麾邵陵王長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Yueyang, Xuan yuan, with charge of the princely administration—but before he took up the post was transferred as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, Yunhui, and Governor of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was named chief clerk to Prince Xuanyuan of Yueyang with charge of the princely household, but before he assumed the post was shifted to chief clerk to Prince Yunhui of Shaoling and governor of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 大同九年，王遷鎮郢州，除平西諮議參軍，加戎昭將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong the prince was reassigned to garrison Yingzhou; Xian was made Military Advisor for Pacifying the West with promotion to General of Martial Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year nine the prince was reassigned to garrison Yingzhou; Xian became military advisor for pacifying the west with the rank of General of Martial Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 友人劉之遴啓皇太子曰：「之遴嘗聞，夷、叔、柳惠，不逢仲尼一言，則西山餓夫，東國黜士，名豈施於後世。

translations.literal: His friend Liu Zhilin memorialized the Crown Prince: “Zhilin has heard that Boyi, Shuqi, and Liuxia Hui—had Confucius not spoken a word, they would have been starving men of the western hills, disgraced scholars of the eastern state; would their names have reached later ages?
translations.idiomatic: His friend Liu Zhilin wrote to the crown prince: “Zhilin has heard that Boyi, Shuqi, and Liuxia Hui—without a word from Confucius—would have been starving men on the western hills, humbled scholars in the eastern state; would their names have lived on?

sentences.zh: 信哉！

translations.literal: So it is true!
translations.idiomatic: Truly so!

sentences.zh: 生有七尺之形，終爲一棺之土。

translations.literal: Born with a body seven feet tall, in the end one coffin’s earth.
translations.idiomatic: A body seven feet high is born; in the end it fills but one coffin of earth.

sentences.zh: 不朽之事，寄之題目，懷珠抱玉，有歿世而名不稱者，可爲長太息，孰過於斯。

translations.literal: What outlasts death is entrusted to words on the page; those who clasp pearl and jade yet go nameless when they die—what sigh can be longer? And who more so than this?
translations.idiomatic: Immortality is left to what is written; those who hold pearl and jade may still die without a name—what grief is deeper? And who deeper than this?

sentences.zh: 竊痛友人沛國劉顯，韞櫝藝文，研精覃奧，聰明特達，出類拔羣。

translations.literal: I grieve that my friend Liu Xian of Pei, his literary gifts wrapped close as gems in a casket, delving to the depths of the profound, with singular intelligence surpassing his kind—
translations.idiomatic: I mourn my friend Liu Xian of Pei, who hoarded learning like gems in a casket, plumbed the deepest texts, and with rare brilliance stood above his peers—

sentences.zh: 闔棺郢都，歸魂上國，卜宅有日，須鐫墓板。

translations.literal: The coffin closed in Ying’s capital, his soul returning to the upper realm; the day to fix his grave approaches and the tomb tablet must be carved.
translations.idiomatic: His coffin was closed in the capital of Ying, his soul returning to the upper land; the day to choose his grave is near, and the tomb stone must be cut.

sentences.zh: 之遴已略撰其事行，今輒上呈。

translations.literal: Zhilin has already drafted an account of his conduct and now respectfully submits it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilin has already drafted his life’s record and now respectfully presents it.

sentences.zh: 伏願鴻慈，降茲睿藻，榮其枯骴，以慰幽魂。

translations.literal: I bow that your vast grace may descend in luminous composition, to honor these dry bones and comfort a shadow soul.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that your vast mercy may grant luminous words, to grace these dry bones and comfort a shade in the dark.

sentences.zh: 冒昧塵聞，戰慄無地。

translations.literal: Presuming to raise this dust before your hearing, I tremble without a place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Daring to trouble your hearing with this dust, I tremble and know not where to stand.

sentences.zh: 」乃蒙令爲誌銘曰：「繁弱挺質，空桑吐聲，分器見重，播樂傳名。

translations.literal: He received an order for an inscription: “When Fanruo drew its nature from emptiness, Kongsang gave forth its tone—distributed, vessels gained weight; spread abroad, music and fame endure.
translations.idiomatic: He received an order to compose the epitaph: “When the strong bow drew substance from the void, the hollow mulberry gave forth its sound—once the vessel was allotted, it was prized; once the music spread, its name endured.

sentences.zh: 誰其均之？

translations.literal: Who balanced such things?
translations.idiomatic: Who held the balance?

sentences.zh: 美有髦士。

translations.literal: There was a brilliant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: There was a splendid gentleman.

sentences.zh: 禮著幼年，業明壯齒。

translations.literal: Rites marked in boyhood, accomplishment clear in mature years.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual showed itself in his youth, mastery in his prime.

sentences.zh: 厭飫典墳，研精名理。

translations.literal: He had his fill of the canonical tomes and plumbed the subtle principles of reason.
translations.idiomatic: He drank deep from the classics and refined his grasp of principle.

sentences.zh: 一見弗忘，過目則記。

translations.literal: Once seen, never forgotten; one pass of the eye and it was fixed in memory.
translations.idiomatic: What he saw once he did not forget; a single glance was enough to lodge it in mind.

sentences.zh: 若訪賈逵，如問伯始。

translations.literal: If you sought Jia Kui, it was as though you had asked Bo Shi himself.
translations.idiomatic: To consult him was like seeking out Jia Kui or putting a question to Bo Shi.

sentences.zh: 穎脫斯出，學優而仕。

translations.literal: He stood out like a head from the husk; learning excellent, then he entered office.
translations.idiomatic: He broke from the sheath of the crowd; his learning was first-rate, and then he served.

sentences.zh: 議獄旣佐，芸蘭乃握。

translations.literal: He aided in deliberating cases, then took up the orchid of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted at the Court of Judicial Review, then held the scholar’s orchid at the National University.

sentences.zh: 摶鳳池水，推羊太學。

translations.literal: He stirred the waters of the Phoenix Pool and led the flock at the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He roiled the Phoenix Pool’s waters and guided the herd at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 內參禁中，外相籓岳。

translations.literal: Within he took part in the forbidden precincts; without he assisted the border princes.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace he advised; beyond it he served the great fiefs.

sentences.zh: 斜光已道，殞彼西浮；

translations.literal: The slanting light has run its course; that western floater has fallen;
translations.idiomatic: The oblique rays have spent their road; yonder sun on the western float has set;

sentences.zh: 百川到海，還逐東流。

translations.literal: All rivers reach the sea, yet still chase the eastern flow.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred streams find the sea, then turn again toward the eastern current.

sentences.zh: 營營返魄，泛泛虛舟。

translations.literal: Restlessly the soul returns; adrift like an empty boat.
translations.idiomatic: The returning soul flutters without rest; he drifts like an empty boat on the flood.

sentences.zh: 白馬向郊，丹旒背鞏。

translations.literal: The white horse turns toward the suburbs; the red banners leave Gong behind.
translations.idiomatic: The white horse faces the outskirts; the crimson pennants turn their backs on Gong.

sentences.zh: 野埃興伏，山雲輕重。

translations.literal: Wild dust rises and settles; mountain clouds grow light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Dust on the plain lifts and subsides; clouds on the hills thicken and thin.

sentences.zh: 呂掩書墳，揚歸玄塚。

translations.literal: Lü covers the grave of books; Yang returns to the dark mound.
translations.idiomatic: Like Lü, he buries learning in the tomb; like Yang, he goes home to the hidden barrow.

sentences.zh: 爾其戒行，途窮土壟。

translations.literal: Take heed in your going; the road ends at the earthen ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Guard your steps on the way; the path runs out at the heaped earth.

sentences.zh: 弱葛方施，叢柯日拱。

translations.literal: Tender creepers have only begun to spread; thick trunks day by day arch overhead.
translations.idiomatic: Weak vines are just now put forth; clustered boughs daily bow and close.

sentences.zh: 鹆遂柳荑春，禽寒斂氄。

translations.literal: The year follows willow catkins in spring; in the cold, birds draw in their down.
translations.idiomatic: Spring comes with willow down; in the chill, birds tuck their feathers close.

sentences.zh: 長空常暗，陰泉獨湧。

translations.literal: The long sky stays dark; only the yin-spring wells up alone.
translations.idiomatic: The wide heavens remain dim; in the underworld spring alone still surges.

sentences.zh: 祔彼故塋，流芬相踵。」

translations.literal: Place him beside that old grave; fragrance flows on in succession.”
translations.idiomatic: Lay him by that ancient mound; let fragrance pass from hand to hand.”

sentences.zh: 顯有三子：莠，荏，臻。

translations.literal: Xian had three sons: You, Ren, and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had three sons—You, Ren, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 臻早著名。

translations.literal: Zhen early won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was famed from early on.

sentences.zh: 劉之遴字思貞，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi’li, courtesy name Sizhen, was a native of Nieyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi’li, styled Sizhen, came from Nieyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父虯，齊國子博士，諡文範先生。

translations.literal: His father Qiu was Erudite of the National University in Qi and was posthumously titled Master Wenfan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiu had been Qi’s Erudite of the National University and was honored after death as Master Wenfan.

sentences.zh: 之遴八歲能屬文，十五舉茂才對策，沈約、任昉見而異之。

translations.literal: At eight Zhi’li could compose prose; at fifteen he was presented as a cultivated talent for policy response—Shen Yue and Ren Fang, meeting him, were struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could write essays; at fifteen he was recommended as a cultivated talent for court examination—Shen Yue and Ren Fang marveled when they met him.

sentences.zh: 起家寧朔主簿。

translations.literal: He first entered office as Supporter of the Army for Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: He began service as Supporter of the Army for Pacifying the North.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王瞻嘗候任昉，值之遴在坐，昉謂瞻曰：「此南陽劉之遴，學優未仕，水鏡所宜甄擢。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Zhan once called on Ren Fang and found Zhi’li present; Fang said to Zhan, “This is Liu Zhi’li of Nanyang—his learning is outstanding though he has not yet taken office; the clear mirror of the court ought to lift him up.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan, Minister of Personnel, once visited Ren Fang and found Zhi’li there; Fang told him, “This is Liu Zhi’li of Nanyang—learned and still without a post; the court’s mirror should single him out.

sentences.zh: 」瞻卽辟爲太學博士。

translations.literal: ” Zhan at once recruited him as Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhan immediately summoned him as Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 時張稷新除尚書僕射，托昉爲讓表，昉令之遴代作，操筆立成。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Ji had just been appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and asked Fang to draft his letter of refusal; Fang had Zhi’li write it in his place, and with brush in hand he finished on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji had just become Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and asked Fang to draft a memorial declining the post; Fang had Zhi’li write it, and he finished at once.

sentences.zh: 昉曰：「荊南秀氣，果有異才，後仕必當過僕。

translations.literal: Fang said, “The south of Jing holds fine spirit—truly there is uncommon talent here; in later office he will surely surpass me.
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, “The Jing south breeds bright minds—here is real talent; in time he will outrank me.

sentences.zh: 」御史中丞樂藹，卽之遴舅，憲臺奏彈，皆之遴草焉。

translations.literal: ” Censor-in-Chief Yue Ai was Zhi’li’s maternal uncle; the indictments of the Inspectorate were all drafted by Zhi’li.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yue Ai, Censor-in-Chief, was his uncle on his mother’s side; every memorial of impeachment from the Inspectorate was Zhi’li’s hand.

sentences.zh: 遷平南行參軍，尚書起部郎，延陵令，荊州治中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Aide on the Pacifying-the-South campaign staff, Gentleman in the Ministry of Rites for Establishing Offices, Magistrate of Yanling, and Administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through aide on the Pacifying-the-South staff, Gentleman for Establishing Offices, magistrate of Yanling, and administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗臨荊州，仍遷宣惠記室。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent governed Jingzhou, Zhi’li was moved to Recorder of the Prince’s Household for Propagating Favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor held Jingzhou, he became Recorder of the Prince’s Household for Propagating Favor.

sentences.zh: 之遴篤學明審，博覽羣籍。

translations.literal: Zhi’li was deeply learned and keen in judgment, and ranged widely through the canon.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi’li studied with fierce devotion and clear discernment, and read broadly in every book.

sentences.zh: 時劉顯、韋稜並強記，之遴每與討論，咸不能過也。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Xian and Wei Ling both had powerful memories; whenever Zhi’li debated with them, none could get the better of him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian and Wei Ling were both famed for recall; in every disputation with Zhi’li, neither could prevail.

sentences.zh: 還除通直散騎侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: On return he was made Regular Attendant with Unimpeded Access and concurrently Palace Secretariat Attendant for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became Regular Attendant with unimpeded access and also a palace secretariat attendant for general affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷正員郎，尚書右丞，荊州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Attendant, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Chief Evaluator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and chief evaluator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎，鴻臚卿，復兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: In succession he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, Minister of Ceremonies, and again concurrently Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Secretariat gentleman, Minister of Ceremonies, and again palace secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲征西鄱陽王長史、南郡太守，高祖謂曰：「卿母年德並高，故令卿衣錦還鄉，盡榮養之理。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Pacifying-the-West in Poyang and Governor of Nan Commandery; the Founding Emperor said to him, “Your mother is advanced in years and in virtue alike—therefore I send you home in splendor to fulfill every duty of honor and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as chief clerk to the Pacifying-the-West Prince of Poyang and governor of Nan Commandery; the Founding Emperor told him, “Your mother is high in years and in virtue—so I send you home in glory to perform every rite of filial nurture.

sentences.zh: 」後轉爲西中郎湘東王長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: ” Later he was transferred as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Western Central in Xiangdong, keeping his governorship as before.
translations.idiomatic: ” Later he became chief clerk to the Western Central Prince of Xiangdong, retaining the governorship.

sentences.zh: 初，之遴在荊府，嘗寄居南郡廨，忽夢前太守袁彖謂曰：「卿後當爲折臂太守，卽居此中。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Zhi’li was on the staff in Jingzhou, he had lodged in the Nan Commandery yamen; suddenly he dreamed that the former governor Yuan Can said to him, “You will later be the one-armed governor and will dwell in this very place.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on Jingzhou staff, he lodged in the Nan Commandery offices and dreamed the former governor Yuan Can said, “You will one day be the broken-armed governor and live here.

sentences.zh: 」之遴後果損臂，遂臨此郡。

translations.literal: ” Zhi’li later did injure his arm and indeed came to govern that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: ” He later lost the use of an arm and in fact took that post.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，徵秘書監，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When his mother died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was summoned as Director of the Palace Library, with concurrent rank as Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother’s death he mourned; when the mourning was done he was called back as Director of the Palace Library and Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 出爲郢州行事，之遴意不願出，固辭，高祖手敕曰：「朕聞妻子具，孝衰於親；

translations.literal: He went out as Acting Governor of Yingzhou; Zhi’li was unwilling to leave the capital and firmly declined—whereupon the Founding Emperor wrote in his own hand: “We have heard that when wife and children are provided for, filial devotion toward parents declines;
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as acting governor of Yingzhou; Zhi’li did not wish to go and refused firmly—the Founding Emperor wrote by his own hand, “We hear that when wife and children are complete, love for parents wanes;

sentences.zh: 爵祿具，忠衰於君。

translations.literal: when rank and salary are complete, loyalty toward one’s lord declines.
translations.idiomatic: when rank and stipend are complete, loyalty to one’s lord wanes.

sentences.zh: 卿旣內足，理忘奉公之節。

translations.literal: You are already full within—by rights you have forgotten the duty of serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: You are already full within—and so, it seems, you have set aside the duty of public service.

sentences.zh: 」遂爲有司所奏免。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the authorities memorialized and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The authorities memorialized against him and he was removed.

sentences.zh: 久之，爲太府卿，都官尚書，太常卿。

translations.literal: After a long while he served as Minister of the Palace Treasuries, Minister Director of Justice, and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he became Minister of the Palace Treasuries, Minister Director of Justice, and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 之遴好古愛奇，在荊州聚古器數十百種。

translations.literal: Zhi’li loved antiquity and delighted in the strange; in Jingzhou he gathered several tens or hundreds of ancient vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi’li loved the old and cherished the rare; in Jingzhou he collected scores of antique vessels.

sentences.zh: 有一器似甌，可容一斛，上有金錯字，時人無能知者。

translations.literal: There was one vessel like a bowl, able to hold a hu, with inlaid gold characters—no one of the day could read them.
translations.idiomatic: One piece resembled a bowl, held a hu in volume, and bore gold-inlaid script no contemporary could decipher.

sentences.zh: 又獻古器四種於東宮。

translations.literal: He also presented four ancient vessels to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also offered four antiquities to the crown prince’s palace.

sentences.zh: 其第一種，鏤銅鴟夷榼二枚，兩耳有銀鏤，銘云「建平二年造」。

translations.literal: The first kind: two bronze owl-shaped goblets with openwork, silver inlay on both ears, and an inscription reading “Made in the second year of Jianping.”
translations.idiomatic: The first: two openwork bronze owl goblets with silver-inlaid ears, inscribed “Made in the second year of Jianping.”

sentences.zh: 其第二種，金銀錯鏤古樽二枚，有篆銘云「秦容成侯適楚之歲造」。

translations.literal: The second kind: two ancient urns with gold and silver inlay, bearing seal-script inscriptions reading “Made in the year Lord Rongcheng of Qin went south to Chu.”
translations.idiomatic: The second: two antique urns with gold and silver inlay and seal script reading “Made in the year the Lord of Rongcheng of Qin went south to Chu.”

sentences.zh: 其第三種，外國澡灌一口，銘云「元封二年，龜茲國獻」。

translations.literal: The third kind: one foreign bathing ewer, inscribed “In the second year of Yuanfeng, presented by the state of Kucha.”
translations.idiomatic: The third: one foreign bathing ewer, inscribed “Second year of Yuanfeng, presented by Kucha.”

sentences.zh: 其第四種，古制澡盤一枚，銘云「初平二年造」。

translations.literal: The fourth kind: one bathing basin in ancient style, inscribed “Made in the second year of Chuping.”
translations.idiomatic: The fourth: one antique bathing basin, inscribed “Made in the second year of Chuping.”

sentences.zh: 時鄱陽嗣王範得班固所上《漢書》真本，獻之東宮，皇太子令之遴與張纘、到漑、陸襄等參校異同。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Poyang, heir to the title, obtained the authentic manuscript of the Book of Han that Ban Gu submitted; he presented it to the Eastern Palace, and the crown prince ordered Zhi’li, together with Zhang Zuan, Dao Gai, and Lu Xiang, to collate the differences.
translations.idiomatic: The heir to Poyang had obtained Ban Gu’s authentic submission of the Book of Han and sent it to the crown prince, who ordered Zhi’li, Zhang Zuan, Dao Gai, and Lu Xiang to compare variants.

sentences.zh: 之遴具異狀十事，其大略曰：「案古本《漢書》稱『永平十六年五月二十一日己酉，郎班固上』；

translations.literal: Zhi’li set out ten points of difference in full; in outline he said: “According to the ancient Book of Han, it reads, ‘On the twenty-first day of the fifth month of the sixteenth year of Yongping, the twenty-first day jiwei, Gentleman Ban Gu submitted’;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi’li listed ten discrepancies in full; in summary: “The ancient Book of Han reads, ‘On jiwei, the twenty-first day of the fifth month of Yongping year sixteen, Gentleman Ban Gu submitted’;

sentences.zh: 而今本無上書年月日字。

translations.literal: whereas the present text lacks the characters for year, month, and day of submission.
translations.idiomatic: but the present text has no characters for the year, month, and day of submission.

sentences.zh: 又案古本《敘傳》號爲中篇；

translations.literal: Again, the ancient Treatise on the Author is titled the Middle Treatise;
translations.idiomatic: Again, the ancient Author’s Treatise is called the Middle Treatise;

sentences.zh: 今本稱爲《敘傳》。

translations.literal: the present text calls it the Treatise on the Author.
translations.idiomatic: the present text calls it simply the Treatise on the Author.

sentences.zh: 又今本《敘傳》載班彪事行；

translations.literal: Again, the present Treatise on the Author records the conduct of Ban Biao;
translations.idiomatic: Again, the present Treatise on the Author gives Ban Biao’s career;

sentences.zh: 而古本云『稚生彪，自有傳』。

translations.literal: whereas the ancient text says, ‘Biao was born to Ban Zhi; he has his own biography.’
translations.idiomatic: but the ancient text says, ‘Zhi begot Biao, who has his own biography.’

sentences.zh: 又今本紀及表、志、列傳不相合爲次，而古本相合爲次，總成三十八卷。

translations.literal: Again, in the present text the Annals, Tables, Monographs, and Biographies are not arranged in one sequence, whereas in the ancient text they are arranged together, thirty-eight scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the present text does not place Annals, Tables, Treatises, and Biographies in one sequence; the ancient text does, thirty-eight scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 又今本《外戚》在《西域》後；

translations.literal: Again, in the present text the Biography of the Empresses and Consorts comes after the Western Regions;
translations.idiomatic: Again, the present text places the Biography of the Empresses after the Western Regions;

sentences.zh: 古本《外戚》次《帝紀》下。

translations.literal: in the ancient text the Biography of the Empresses follows directly after the Annals.
translations.idiomatic: in the ancient text it follows directly after the Annals.

sentences.zh: 又今本《高五子》、《文三王》、《景十三王》、《武五子》、《宣元六王》雜在諸傳秩中；

translations.literal: Again, in the present text the Five Sons of Gaozu, the Three Kings of Wen, the Thirteen Kings of Jing, the Five Sons of Wu, and the Six Kings of Xuan and Yuan are scattered among the other biographies in order;
translations.idiomatic: Again, the present text scatters the Five Sons of Gaozu, the Three Kings of Wen, the Thirteen Kings of Jing, the Five Sons of Wu, and the Six Kings of Xuan and Yuan among the other ranks of biography;

sentences.zh: 古本諸王悉次《外戚》下，在《陳項傳》前。

translations.literal: in the ancient text all the kings come directly after the Empresses, before the Biographies of Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: in the ancient text all the kings follow the Empresses, before Chen Sheng and Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 又今本《韓彭英盧吳》述云『信惟餓隸，布實黥徒，越亦狗盜，芮尹江湖，雲起龍驤，化爲侯王』；

translations.literal: Again, the present Summaries for Han Xin, Peng Yue, Ying Bu, Lu Wan, and Wu Rui read, “Xin was once a starving menial, Bu a branded convict, Yue a dog-thief, Rui a man of rivers and lakes—clouds rose and dragons soared, and they became marquises and kings”;
translations.idiomatic: Again, the present summary for Han Xin, Peng Yue, Ying Bu, Lu Wan, and Wu Rui reads, “Xin was a starving menial, Bu a branded convict, Yue a dog-thief, Rui of the rivers and lakes—clouds rose, dragons soared, and they became kings and marquises”;

sentences.zh: 古本述云『淮陰毅毅，杖劍周章，邦之傑子，實惟彭、英，化爲侯王，雲起龍驤』。

translations.literal: the ancient Summaries read, “The Marquis of Huaiyin stood bold with sword in hand; Peng and Ying were the state’s heroes; cloud and dragon lifted them, and they became kings and marquises.”
translations.idiomatic: the ancient summary reads, “The Marquis of Huaiyin was bold with sword in hand; Peng and Ying were the realm’s champions; cloud and dragon raised them to kings and marquises.”

sentences.zh: 又古本第三十七卷，解音釋義，以助雅詁，而今本無此卷。」

translations.literal: Again, the ancient text’s thirty-seventh scroll gives pronunciation and glosses to aid the lexicon, whereas the present text lacks this scroll.”
translations.idiomatic: Again, the ancient thirty-seventh scroll gives readings and glosses to aid the lexicon; the present text has no such scroll.”

sentences.zh: 之遴好屬文，多學古體，與河東裴子野、沛國劉顯常共討論書籍，因爲交好。

translations.literal: Zhi’li loved to compose prose and often wrote in ancient style; with Pei Ziye of Hedong and Liu Xian of Pei he constantly discussed books and thereby became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi’li loved composition and favored archaic forms; with Pei Ziye of Hedong and Liu Xian of Pei he debated texts until they became intimate friends.

sentences.zh: 是時《周易》、《尚書》、《禮記》、《毛詩》並有高祖義疏，惟《左氏傳》尚闕。

translations.literal: At that time the Changes, Documents, Record of Rites, and Mao Odes all had exegeses composed by the Founding Emperor; only the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn remained without one.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes, Documents, Record of Rites, and Mao Odes all had imperial commentaries; only the Zuo Commentary still lacked one.

sentences.zh: 之遴乃著《春秋大意》十科，《左氏》十科，《三傳同異》十科，合三十事以上之。

translations.literal: Zhi’li thereupon composed ten categories of The Great Meaning of the Spring and Autumn, ten categories of the Zuo Tradition, and ten categories of Agreements and Differences among the Three Commentaries—thirty topics in all—and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote ten topics on the Great Meaning of the Spring and Autumn, ten on the Zuo Tradition, and ten on agreements and differences among the three commentaries—thirty in all—and presented them.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，詔答之曰：「省所撰《春秋》義，比事論書，辭微旨遠。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was greatly pleased and answered in an edict: “We have reviewed your Spring and Autumn exegesis: events compared and books weighed, the wording subtle and the aim far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor was delighted and replied by edict: “We have read your Spring and Autumn exegesis—events set side by side, books weighed, language fine and purpose far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 編年之教，言闡義繁，丘明傳洙泗之風，公羊稟西河之學，鐸椒之解不追，瑕丘之說無取。

translations.literal: The annalistic teaching speaks broadly and the meaning is intricate; Qiu Ming transmitted the wind of Zhu and Si, Gongsun bore the learning of the western river—the explanations of Duo and Jiao do not reach it, the discourse of Xiqiu has nothing to take.
translations.idiomatic: Annalistic teaching is wide in utterance and rich in meaning; Qiu Ming carried the breath of Zhu and Si, Gongsun drew the learning of the western river—Duo and Jiao cannot catch up, Xiqiu’s sayings have nothing worth taking.

sentences.zh: 繼踵胡母，仲舒云盛，因循《穀梁》，千秋最篤。

translations.literal: Following in the steps of Humu, Dong Zhongshu flourished; along the line of the Guliang, Gongsun Qian was most steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: After Humu, Dong Zhongshu rose; along the Guliang line, Gongsun Qian was most firm.

sentences.zh: 張蒼之傳《左氏》，賈誼之襲荀卿，源本分鑣，指歸殊致，詳略紛然，其來舊矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Cang transmitted the Zuo Tradition; Jia Yi inherited Xun Qing—the sources parted like wheel-ruts, the bearings diverged, detail and summary tangled together, and so it has been since old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cang handed on the Zuo Tradition; Jia Yi took up Xun Qing—the springs forked, the bearings differed, detail and summary in disarray, as it has long been.

sentences.zh: 昔在弱年，乃經研味，一從遺置，迄將五紀。

translations.literal: In my weak years I once studied and savored it, but once cast aside it has now drawn near five twelve-year cycles.
translations.idiomatic: In my youth I once studied and tasted it, but once set aside it has now neared five twelve-year cycles.

sentences.zh: 兼晚冬晷促，機事罕暇，夜分求衣，未遑搜括。

translations.literal: Moreover the late-winter sun is brief and business rarely leaves leisure; at midnight I seek my robe and have no time to search and gather.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover late winter shortens the day and affairs leave little leisure; at midnight I reach for my robe and have no time to hunt and collate.

sentences.zh: 須待夏景，試取推尋，若溫故可求，別酬所問也。」

translations.literal: I must wait for summer light, try a fresh review and inquiry—if the old can be recovered by warming, I shall repay your question in another way.”
translations.idiomatic: Wait till summer light, then I shall try review and inquiry—if the old learning can be found by warming, I shall answer your question another way.”

sentences.zh: 太清二年，侯景亂，之遴避難還鄉，未至，卒於夏口，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taqing, when Hou Jing rebelled, Zhi’li fled homeward to escape the turmoil; before he arrived he died at Xiakou, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Taqing year two, as Hou Jing’s rebellion spread, Zhi’li fled home but died at Xiakou before he arrived, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 前後文集五十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings before and after, fifty scrolls, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, fifty scrolls in all, circulated abroad.

sentences.zh: 之亨字嘉會，之遴弟也。

translations.literal: Zhiheng, courtesy name Jiahui, was Zhi’li’s younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiheng, styled Jiahui, was Zhi’li’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少有令名。

translations.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed from youth.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，拜太學博士，稍遷兼中書通事舍人，步兵校尉，司農卿。

translations.literal: He was presented as a cultivated talent, appointed Erudite of the National University, and in time was promoted to concurrent Palace Secretariat Attendant for General Affairs, Commandant of Footsoldiers, and Minister of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Presented as a cultivated talent, he became Erudite of the National University, then palace secretariat attendant, Commandant of Footsoldiers, and Minister of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 又代兄之遴爲安西湘東王長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: He also replaced his elder brother Zhi’li as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Pacifying-the-West in Xiangdong and Governor of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He also succeeded his brother as chief clerk to the Pacifying-the-West Prince of Xiangdong and governor of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 在郡有異績。

translations.literal: In the commandery his achievements were outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: In office his record was exceptional.

sentences.zh: 數年卒于官，時年五十。

translations.literal: After several years he died in post, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he died in office, at fifty.

sentences.zh: 荊士至今懷之，不忍斥其名，號爲「大南郡」、「小南郡」云。

translations.literal: The people of Jing still cherish them and cannot bear to speak their given names, calling them instead “the Greater Nan Commandery” and “the Lesser Nan Commandery.”
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jing still honor them and will not speak their personal names, calling them only “the Greater Nan Commandery” and “the Lesser Nan Commandery.”

sentences.zh: 許懋字昭哲，高陽新城人，魏鎮北將軍允九世孫。

translations.literal: Xu Mao, courtesy name Zhaozhe, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang, ninth-generation descendant of Xu Yun, General Who Pacifies the North of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mao, styled Zhaozhe, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang, ninth in descent from Xu Yun, Wei’s General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 祖珪，宋給事中，著作郎，桂陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was Attendant in the Secretariat of Song, Gentleman of the Palace Library, and Governor of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui had been Song’s secretariat attendant, palace library gentleman, and governor of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 父勇惠，齊太子家令，冗從僕射。

translations.literal: His father Yonghui was Household Steward to the Heir Apparent of Qi and Supernumerary Attendant of the Suite.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yonghui was Qi’s household steward to the heir apparent and supernumerary attendant of the suite.

sentences.zh: 懋少孤，性至孝，居父憂，執喪過禮。

translations.literal: Mao lost his father early and was filial to the utmost; while observing mourning for his father he exceeded the rites in his grief.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was orphaned young and filial to the bone; in mourning for his father he went beyond the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 篤志好學，爲州黨所稱。

translations.literal: He set his will on study and was praised by his district.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to learning and was praised throughout his district.

sentences.zh: 十四入太學，受《毛詩》，旦領師說，晚而覆講，座下聽者常數十百人，因撰《風雅比興義》十五卷，盛行於世。

translations.literal: At fourteen he entered the National University and studied the Mao Odes; mornings he received the master’s teaching, evenings he lectured in return, and those seated below him to listen often numbered in the tens or hundreds—thereby he composed Parallels of Style and Meaning in fifteen scrolls, which flourished in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered the National University to study the Mao Odes; by day he heard the master, by night he lectured in turn, with scores of listeners below—and so he wrote Parallels of Style and Meaning in fifteen scrolls, widely read in his day.

sentences.zh: 尤曉故事，稱爲儀注之學。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in precedent and was called a master of ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He knew precedent especially well and was styled a master of ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 起家後軍豫章王行參軍，轉法曹，舉茂才，遷驃騎大將軍儀同中記室。

translations.literal: He first entered office as Aide on the campaign staff of the Prince of Yuzhang in the Rear Army, was transferred to the Law Bureau, was presented as a cultivated talent, and was promoted to Recorder in the Secretariat of the General of Agile Cavalry with Equal Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He began as aide on the Rear Army staff of the Prince of Yuzhang, moved to the law bureau, was presented as a cultivated talent, and rose to recorder in the secretariat of the General of Agile Cavalry with Equal Protocol.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子聞而召之，侍講于崇明殿，除太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent Wen Hui heard of him he summoned him to lecture at Chongming Hall and appointed him Commandant of Footsoldiers to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wen Hui summoned him to lecture at Chongming Hall and made him Commandant of Footsoldiers to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 永元中，轉散騎侍郎，兼國子博士。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he was transferred to Regular Attendant and concurrently Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongyuan he became Regular Attendant and also Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 與司馬褧同志友善，僕射江祏甚推重之，號爲「經史笥」。

translations.literal: He was of one mind and close friendship with Sima Jiong; Vice Director Jiang Shi greatly esteemed him and called him “the casket of classics and histories.”
translations.idiomatic: He was intimate with Sima Jiong; Vice Director Jiang Shi prized him and called him “the casket of canon and history.”

sentences.zh: 天監初，吏部尚書范雲舉懋參詳五禮，除征西鄱陽王諮議，兼著作郎，待詔文德省。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tianjian, Minister of Personnel Fan Yun recommended Mao to assist in compiling the Five Rites; he was appointed Advisor to the Prince of Pacifying-the-West in Poyang, with concurrent service as Gentleman of the Palace Library, awaiting edicts at the Wende Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjian opened, Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, recommended Mao to help shape the Five Rites; he became advisor to the Pacifying-the-West Prince of Poyang, also palace library gentleman, awaiting edicts at the Wende Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時有請封會稽禪國山者，高祖雅好禮，因集儒學之士，草封禪儀，將欲行焉。

translations.literal: At that time some petitioned to enfeoff Mount Kuaiji and perform the Feng and Shan rites on Mount Guoshan; the Founding Emperor by nature loved ritual, and so he gathered Confucian scholars to draft the rites of enfeoffment and Feng and Shan, intending to carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: Some then petitioned to enfeoff Mount Kuaiji and perform Feng and Shan on Mount Guoshan; the Founding Emperor, a lover of ritual, gathered Confucian scholars to draft the ceremonies and meant to perform them.

sentences.zh: 懋以爲不可，因建議曰：

translations.literal: Mao held it inadmissible and submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Mao judged it impossible and memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣案舜幸岱宗，是爲巡狩，而鄭引《孝經鉤命決》云「封于泰山，考績柴燎，禪乎梁甫，刻石紀號」。

translations.literal: Your servant finds that when Shun visited Dai, it was a tour of inspection; yet Zheng cites the Weft of the Classic of Filial Piety, Apocryphal Decisions: “He enfeoffed at Mount Tai, examined merit with a firewood offering, performed Shan at Mount Liangfu, and carved stone to record his title.”
translations.idiomatic: I find Shun’s visit to Dai was a royal tour of inspection; yet Zheng Xuan cites the apocryphal Hooking Life Decisions on the Classic of Filial Piety: “Enfeoffment at Mount Tai, merit reviewed with a firewood offering, Shan at Mount Liangfu, stone carved to record the title.”

sentences.zh: 此緯書之曲說，非正經之通義也。

translations.literal: These are tortuous readings of apocryphal weft-texts, not the settled sense of the orthodox classics.
translations.idiomatic: That is a forced reading from weft apocrypha, not the plain meaning of the canonical classics.

sentences.zh: 依《白虎通》云，「封者，言附廣也；

translations.literal: According to the Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall, “Feng means to enlarge what is attached;
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall says, “Feng means to enlarge what is joined;

sentences.zh: 禪者，言成功相傳也」。

translations.literal: Shan means to hand on success.”
translations.idiomatic: Shan means to transmit achievement.”

sentences.zh: 若以禪授爲義，則禹不應傳啓至桀十七世也，湯又不應傳外丙至紂三十七世也。

translations.literal: If Shan is taken to mean ceding the throne, then Yu ought not to have passed the line from Qi to Jie through seventeen reigns, nor Tang from Wai Bing to Zhou through thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: If Shan meant abdication, Yu would not have passed the throne from Qi to Jie across seventeen reigns, nor Tang from Wai Bing to Zhou across thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 又《禮記》云：「三皇禪奕奕，謂盛德也。

translations.literal: Again the Record of Rites says: “The Three Sovereigns performed Shan with exuberant ease—meaning their overflowing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites also says: “The Three Sovereigns’ Shan was exuberant ease”—that is, overflowing virtue.

sentences.zh: 五帝禪亭亭，特立獨起於身也。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors performed Shan with lofty uprightness—meaning they stood alone and rose by their own persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors’ Shan was lofty uprightness”—they stood alone and rose by their own merit.

sentences.zh: 三王禪梁甫，連延不絕，父沒子繼也。

translations.literal: The Three Kings performed Shan at Mount Liangfu—meaning unbroken succession, father dying and son succeeding.”
translations.idiomatic: The Three Kings’ Shan was at Mount Liangfu”—unbroken succession, father dead and son following.”

sentences.zh: 」若謂「禪奕奕爲盛德者，古義以伏羲、神農、黃帝，是爲三皇。

translations.literal: ” If “Shan with exuberant ease” is said to mean overflowing virtue, the ancient sense takes Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor as the Three Sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: ” If “exuberant ease” meant overflowing virtue, antiquity counted Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor as the Three Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 伏羲封泰山，禪云云，黃帝封泰山，禪亭亭，皆不禪奕奕，而云盛德，則無所寄矣。

translations.literal: Fuxi performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at such-and-such a place; the Yellow Emperor performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan with lofty uprightness—neither performed Shan with exuberant ease, yet if one speaks of overflowing virtue, there is nothing to which it can attach.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi enfeoffed at Mount Tai and performed Shan at such-and-such a hill; the Yellow Emperor enfeoffed at Mount Tai and Shan with lofty uprightness—neither used “exuberant ease,” so “overflowing virtue” has nowhere to lodge.

sentences.zh: 若謂五帝禪亭亭，特立獨起於身者，顓頊封泰山，禪云云，帝嚳封泰山，禪云云，堯封泰山，禪云云，舜封泰山，禪云云，亦不禪亭亭，若合黃帝以爲五帝者，少昊卽黃帝子，又非獨立之義矣。

translations.literal: If the Five Emperors’ “Shan with lofty uprightness” means standing alone and rising by one’s own person, Zhuanxu performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at such-and-such a place; Emperor Ku, Yao, and Shun did the same—none performed Shan with lofty uprightness. If the Yellow Emperor is counted among the Five Emperors, Shaohao was the Yellow Emperor’s son, which again is not the sense of standing alone.
translations.idiomatic: If the Five Emperors’ “lofty uprightness” meant standing alone, Zhuanxu, Ku, Yao, and Shun all enfeoffed at Mount Tai and performed Shan at such-and-such hills—none with “lofty uprightness.” Count the Yellow Emperor among the Five and Shaohao was his son—hardly “standing alone.”

sentences.zh: 若謂三王禪梁甫，連延不絕，父沒子繼者，禹封泰山，禪云云，周成王封泰山，禪社首，舊書如此，異乎《禮說》，皆道聽所得，失其本文。

translations.literal: If the Three Kings’ Shan at Mount Liangfu means unbroken succession, father dead and son succeeding, Yu performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at such-and-such a place; King Cheng of Zhou performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at Mount Sheshou—as old books have it, differing from the Ritual Explanations; all are hearsay, having lost the original text.
translations.idiomatic: If the Three Kings’ Shan at Mount Liangfu meant unbroken father-to-son succession, Yu enfeoffed at Mount Tai and performed Shan elsewhere; Zhou King Cheng enfeoffed at Mount Tai and Shan at Mount Sheshou—so the old books say, unlike the Ritual Explanations: hearsay all, the originals lost.

sentences.zh: 假使三王皆封泰山禪梁甫者，是爲封泰山則有傳世之義，禪梁甫則有揖讓之懷，或欲禪位，或欲傳子，義旣矛盾，理必不然。

translations.literal: Suppose all Three Kings performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at Mount Liangfu: then Feng at Mount Tai would carry the sense of handing on the world, while Shan at Mount Liangfu would carry the intent of yielding the throne—whether one wished to abdicate or to pass the throne to a son, the meanings contradict one another; reason cannot allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose every Three King enfeoffed at Mount Tai and performed Shan at Mount Liangfu: Feng would mean handing on the realm, Shan at Liangfu would mean yielding the throne—abdicate or bequeath to a son, the senses clash; it cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 又七十二君，夷吾所記，此中世數，裁可得二十餘主：伏羲、神農、女媧、大庭、柏皇、中央、栗陸、驪連、赫胥、尊盧、混沌、昊英、有巢、硃襄、葛天、陰康、無懷、黃帝、少昊、顓頊、高辛、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，中間乃有共工，霸有九州，非帝之數，云何得有七十二君封禪之事？

translations.literal: Again, the seventy-two rulers recorded by Guan Zhong—among these middle antiquity can yield only a little more than twenty lords: Fuxi, Shennong, Nüwa, Dating, Baihuang, Zhongyang, Lilu, Lilian, Hexu, Zunlu, Hundun, Haoying, Youchao, Zhuxiang, Getian, Yinkang, Wuhuai, the Yellow Emperor, Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Gaoxin, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu—in the middle there was even Gonggong, who dominated the Nine Provinces as a hegemon, not an emperor’s number; how could there have been seventy-two rulers performing Feng and Shan?
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong’s seventy-two rulers, counted soberly, yield barely twenty-odd names—Fuxi through Wu, with Gonggong hegemon of the Nine Provinces in between, no emperor’s tally: whence seventy-two Feng-and-Shan kings?

sentences.zh: 且燧人以前至周之世，未有君臣，人心淳樸，不應金泥玉檢，升中刻石。

translations.literal: Moreover, from before the Fire-Drillers down to the Zhou age there were not yet ruler and minister; hearts were plain and simple—one should not speak of gold paste and jade cases, ascending the central peak and carving stone.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Fire-Drillers through Zhou there was no ruler-and-minister order and hearts were plain—gold paste, jade cases, ascent of the central peak, and carved stone do not belong there.

sentences.zh: 燧人、伏羲、神農三皇結繩而治，書契未作，未應有鐫文告成。

translations.literal: The Fire-Drillers, Fuxi, and Shennong, the Three Sovereigns, governed by knotted cords; writing was not yet made—one should not speak of carving characters to announce completion.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Sovereigns—Fire-Drillers, Fuxi, Shennong—ruled by knotted cords before script existed; carved characters proclaiming completion are out of place.

sentences.zh: 且無懷氏，伏羲後第十六主，云何得在伏羲前封泰山禪云云？

translations.literal: Moreover, Wuhuai was the sixteenth ruler after Fuxi—how could he have performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at such-and-such a place before Fuxi?
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuai was Fuxi’s sixteenth successor—how could he enfeoff at Mount Tai and perform Shan before Fuxi?

sentences.zh: 夷吾又曰：「惟受命之君然後得封禪。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong also said: “Only a ruler who has received the mandate may perform Feng and Shan.”
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong also said, “Only a mandate-bearing ruler may perform Feng and Shan.”

sentences.zh: 」周成王非受命君，云何而得封泰山禪社首？

translations.literal: ” King Cheng of Zhou was not a mandate-receiving ruler—how could he perform Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at Mount Sheshou?
translations.idiomatic: ” King Cheng of Zhou did not receive the mandate—how could he enfeoff at Mount Tai and perform Shan at Mount Sheshou?

sentences.zh: 神農與炎帝是一主，而云神農封泰山禪云云，炎帝封泰山禪云云，分爲二人，妄亦甚矣！

translations.literal: Shennong and the Flame Emperor were one lord, yet the text says Shennong performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at such-and-such a place, and the Flame Emperor performed Feng at Mount Tai and Shan at such-and-such a place—split into two men; the error is extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Shennong and the Flame Emperor were one sovereign, yet the record splits them into two who each enfeoffed at Mount Tai and performed Shan—an egregious fiction.

sentences.zh: 若是聖主，不須封禪；

translations.literal: If they were sage rulers, Feng and Shan were unnecessary;
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers had no need of Feng and Shan;

sentences.zh: 若是凡主，不應封禪。

translations.literal: if they were ordinary rulers, they ought not to perform Feng and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: ordinary rulers ought not to attempt them.

sentences.zh: 當是齊桓欲行此事，管仲知其不可，故舉怪物以屈之也。

translations.literal: Surely Duke Huan of Qi wished to carry out this affair; Guan Zhong knew it could not be done and therefore raised prodigies to bend his will.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi wished to do it; Guan Zhong knew it impossible and piled up marvels to turn him aside.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇登泰山中阪，風雨暴至，休松樹下，封爲五大夫，而事不遂。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang, ascending Mount Tai midway, was met by a sudden storm; he rested beneath a pine and enfeoffed it as one of the Five Great Officers, yet the rite was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang climbed halfway up Mount Tai when wind and rain burst upon him; he sheltered under a pine, enfeoffed it as a Great Officer of the fifth rank, and still the rite failed.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝宗信方士，廣召儒生，皮弁搢紳，射牛行事，獨與霍嬗俱上，旣而子侯暴卒，厥足用傷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han trusted the recipes of the masters of methods, broadly summoned Confucians, donned the leather cap and inserted the girdle-pin, shot the ox in the rite, and went up alone with Huo Shang; soon after, Zihou died suddenly and the emperor injured his foot.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi believed the recipe masters, summoned Confucians in leather caps and pinned sashes, shot the ox in the rite, and ascended with Huo Shang alone; soon Zihou died suddenly and the emperor hurt his foot.

sentences.zh: 至魏明，使高堂隆撰其禮儀，聞隆沒，歎息曰：「天不欲成吾事，高生舍我亡也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming of Wei, Gao Tanglong was ordered to draft the ritual protocols; when Long died, the emperor sighed, “Heaven does not wish my affair to succeed—Master Gao has left me in death.”
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi had Gao Tanglong draft the rites; when Long died the emperor sighed, “Heaven will not let me finish—Gao has left me.”

sentences.zh: 」晉武泰始中欲封禪，乃至太康議猶不定，意不果行。

translations.literal: ” In the Taishi era of Jin Wu the court wished to perform Feng and Shan; even in the Taikang deliberations it was still unsettled, and in the end the intent was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jin Wudi in Taishi meant to perform Feng and Shan; debate still ran at Taikang, and the rite never came off.

sentences.zh: 孫皓遣兼司空董朝、兼太常周處至陽羨封禪國山。

translations.literal: Sun Hao sent Acting Minister of Works Dong Chao and Acting Minister of Rites Zhou Chu to Yangxian to perform Feng and Shan at Mount Guoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao sent Acting Minister of Works Dong Chao and Acting Minister of Rites Zhou Chu to Yangxian to enfeoff Mount Guoshan and perform Feng and Shan.

sentences.zh: 此朝君子，有何功德？

translations.literal: What merit had these court gentlemen of Wu?
translations.idiomatic: What merit had these gentlemen of Wu?

sentences.zh: 不思古道而欲封禪，皆是主好名於上，臣阿旨於下也。

translations.literal: To ignore the ancient way and wish for Feng and Shan—in every case the ruler above craves a name and the ministers below flatter his intent.
translations.idiomatic: To spurn the ancient way and seek Feng and Shan is always the ruler’s hunger for fame above and the ministers’ flattery below.

sentences.zh: 夫封禪者，不出正經，惟《左傳》說「禹會諸侯於塗山，執玉帛者萬國」，亦不謂爲封禪。

translations.literal: Feng and Shan do not appear in the orthodox classics; only the Zuo Commentary says that “Yu assembled the feudal lords at Mount Tu, and those bearing jade and silk numbered ten thousand states”—and even that is not called Feng and Shan.
