translations.idiomatic: Feng and Shan are not in the orthodox classics; only the Zuo Commentary has Yu assembling the lords at Mount Tu with ten thousand states bearing jade and silk—and even that is not called Feng and Shan.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄有參、柴之風，不能推尋正經，專信緯候之書，斯爲謬矣。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan had the manner of Shen and Zhai in sacrifice, yet could not trace the orthodox classics and trusted only the weft apocrypha and prognostic texts—here he erred.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan had Shen and Zhai’s sacrificial manner yet could not search the classics and trusted only weft apocrypha and prognostic books—there he went wrong.

sentences.zh: 蓋《禮》云「因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土享帝于郊」。

translations.literal: The Rites say, “Because of Heaven, serve Heaven; because of Earth, serve Earth; because of famous mountains, ascend the central peak to Heaven; because of auspicious earth, enjoy the Emperor in the suburbs.”
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: “Because of Heaven, serve Heaven; because of Earth, serve Earth; because of famous mountains, ascend the central peak toward Heaven; because of auspicious earth, enjoy the Emperor in the suburbs.”

sentences.zh: 燔柴岱宗，卽因山之謂矣。

translations.literal: Burning firewood at Dai—that is what “because of mountains” means.
translations.idiomatic: Burning firewood at Dai is precisely “because of mountains.”

sentences.zh: 故《曲禮》云「天子祭天地」是也。

translations.literal: Thus the Summary of the Rites says, “The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth”—that is the sense.
translations.idiomatic: So the Summary of the Rites: “The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth”—that is it.

sentences.zh: 又祈穀一，報穀一，禮乃不顯祈報地，推文則有。

translations.literal: Again there is one prayer for grain and one thanksgiving for grain; in the rites the prayer and thanksgiving to Earth are not displayed, yet by extension of the text they exist.
translations.idiomatic: There is also one prayer for grain and one thanksgiving for grain; the rites do not spell out prayer and thanksgiving to Earth, yet the text implies them.

sentences.zh: 《樂記》云：「大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節；

translations.literal: The Record of Music says: “Great music is in harmony with Heaven; great rites are in rhythm with Earth;
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Music says, “Great music harmonizes with Heaven; great rites keep rhythm with Earth;

sentences.zh: 和故百物不失，節故祀天祭地。

translations.literal: in harmony, the hundred things are not lost; in rhythm, Heaven is sacrificed to and Earth is sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: in harmony the hundred things are not lost; in rhythm Heaven is sacrificed to and Earth is sacrificed to.”

sentences.zh: 」百物不失者，天生之，地養之。

translations.literal: ” That the hundred things are not lost means Heaven gives birth and Earth nourishes.
translations.idiomatic: ” “The hundred things are not lost” means Heaven gives birth and Earth nourishes.

sentences.zh: 故知地亦有祈報，是則一年三郊天，三祭地。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that Earth also has prayer and thanksgiving; in all there are three suburban sacrifices to Heaven and three sacrifices to Earth in a year.
translations.idiomatic: So Earth too has prayer and thanksgiving: three suburban sacrifices to Heaven and three to Earth in a year.

sentences.zh: 《周官》有員丘方澤者，總爲三事，郊祭天地。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou have the round mound and the square marsh—taken together these are three affairs, suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou have the round mound and the square marsh—three rites in all, suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 故《小宗伯》云「兆五帝於四郊」，此卽《月令》迎氣之郊也。

translations.literal: Thus the Minister of the Lesser Ancestral Temple says, “Take omens for the Five Emperors in the four suburbs”—this is the suburban reception of the seasonal qi from the Monthly Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Lesser Ancestral Temple says, “Take omens for the Five Emperors in the four suburbs”—the seasonal suburban receptions of the Monthly Ordinances.

sentences.zh: 《舜典》有「歲二月東巡狩，至于岱宗」，夏南，秋西，冬北，五年一周，若爲封禪，何其數也！

translations.literal: The Canon of Shun has, “In the second month of the year, make an eastern tour of inspection, arriving at Dai”—summer south, autumn west, winter north, one circuit in five years; if this were Feng and Shan, how regular the number!
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Shun: “In the second month, tour east to Dai”—then south in summer, west in autumn, north in winter, one circuit in five years; if that were Feng and Shan, how neat the count!

sentences.zh: 此爲九郊，亦皆正義。

translations.literal: These make nine suburban sacrifices, and all are orthodox in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: That makes nine suburban sacrifices, each orthodox in sense.

sentences.zh: 至如大旅於南郊者，非常祭也。

translations.literal: As for the great procession to the southern suburb, it is not a regular sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The great procession to the southern suburb is not a regular sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 《大宗伯》「國有大故則旅上帝」，《月令》云「仲春玄鳥至，祀于高禖」，亦非常祭。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Greater Ancestral Temple: “When the state has a great affair, then process to the Supreme God”; the Monthly Ordinances say, “In mid-spring the dark bird comes—sacrifice at the High Mound”—also not a regular sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Ancestral Temple Minister: “When the state has a great affair, process to the Supreme God”; the Monthly Ordinances: “Mid-spring, the dark bird comes—sacrifice at the High Mound”—also irregular.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》云「克禋克祀，以弗無子」。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes say, “Able in sacrifice, able in worship, that he may not be without sons.”
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, “Able in sacrifice, able in worship, that he may not be without sons.”

sentences.zh: 幷有雩禱，亦非常祭。

translations.literal: There are also the Yu prayer and the rain prayer—again not regular sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu prayer and the rain prayer are also irregular sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 《禮》云「雩，頠水旱也」。

translations.literal: The Rites say, “Yu—prayer in time of drought.”
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say, “Yu—prayer in drought.”

sentences.zh: 是爲合郊天地有三，特郊天有九，非常祀又有三。

translations.literal: Thus, combining suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth there are three; special suburban sacrifices to Heaven alone are nine; irregular sacrifices are again three.
translations.idiomatic: Combined suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth number three; special suburban sacrifices to Heaven alone, nine; irregular sacrifices, three more.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：「宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: “In the Bright Hall, perform the ancestral sacrifice to King Wen to match the Supreme God.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says, “In the Bright Hall, perform the ancestral sacrifice to King Wen to match the Supreme God.”

sentences.zh: 」雩祭與明堂雖是祭天，而不在郊，是爲天祀有十六，地祭有三，惟大禘祀不在此數。

translations.literal: ” The Yu sacrifice and the Bright Hall sacrifice, though sacrifices to Heaven, are not in the suburbs; thus sacrifices to Heaven number sixteen, sacrifices to Earth three, while only the great Di sacrifice is not in this count.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Yu and Bright Hall rites sacrifice to Heaven but not in the suburbs; Heaven sacrifices total sixteen, Earth sacrifices three, and only the great Di sacrifice lies outside this tally.

sentences.zh: 《大傳》云：「王者禘其祖之所自出，以其祖配之。

translations.literal: The Great Tradition says: “The king performs Di to the ancestor from whom his line sprang, matching him with that ancestor.”
translations.idiomatic: The Great Tradition says, “The king performs Di to the ancestor from whom his line sprang, matching him with that ancestor.”

sentences.zh: 」異于常祭，以故云大於時祭。

translations.literal: ” It differs from regular sacrifice; therefore it is said to be greater than the seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: ” It differs from regular sacrifice and is therefore called greater than the seasonal rites.

sentences.zh: 案《繫辭》云：「《易》之爲書也，廣大悉備。

translations.literal: Your servant finds that the Appended Remarks say: “The Changes as a book is broad and great, complete in all respects.
translations.idiomatic: The Appended Remarks say, “The Changes as a book is broad and great, complete in every respect.

sentences.zh: 有天道焉，有地道焉，有人道焉，兼三才而兩之，故六。

translations.literal: There is the Way of Heaven, the Way of Earth, and the Way of Man; joining the three powers and doubling them makes six.
translations.idiomatic: There is the Way of Heaven, the Way of Earth, and the Way of Man; joining the three powers and doubling them yields six.

sentences.zh: 六者非佗，三才之道也。

translations.literal: The six are nothing else but the ways of the three powers.”
translations.idiomatic: The six are nothing but the ways of the three powers.”

sentences.zh: 」《乾·彖》云：「大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Qian Hexagram says: “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! The myriad things owe their beginning to it, and it unifies Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian Commentary says, “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! All things owe their beginning to it, and it unifies Heaven.

sentences.zh: 雲行雨施，品物流形，大明終始，六位時成。

translations.literal: Clouds move and rain is bestowed; the kinds of things take form; the great brightness runs from beginning to end; the six positions are completed in season.”
translations.idiomatic: Clouds move, rain falls; things take shape; the great brightness runs start to finish; the six positions complete themselves in season.”

sentences.zh: 」此則應六年一祭，坤元亦爾。

translations.literal: This corresponds to sacrifice once in six years; the Kun origin is the same.
translations.idiomatic: That answers to sacrifice once in six years; the Kun origin is the same.

sentences.zh: 誠敬之道，盡此而備。

translations.literal: The way of sincerity and reverence is fully provided in this.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity and reverence are fully provided here.

sentences.zh: 至於封禪，非所敢聞。

translations.literal: As for Feng and Shan, your servant does not dare to hear of them.
translations.idiomatic: Of Feng and Shan, your servant dares not speak.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉納之，因推演懋議，稱制旨以答，請者由是遂停。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor praised and accepted it; he then developed Mao’s argument, spoke in the imperial voice to reply, and the petitioners thereby ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor praised and accepted it, developed Mao’s argument, answered in the imperial voice, and the petitioners stopped.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉太子家令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he became Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊舊儀，郊天祀帝，皆用袞冕，至天監七年，懋始請造大裘。

translations.literal: The old rites of Song and Qi for suburban sacrifice to Heaven and enfeoffment of the Emperor all used the dragon robe; only in the seventh year of Tianjian did Mao first request the making of the great fur garment.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Qi used the dragon robe for suburban sacrifice to Heaven and for enfeoffing the Emperor; only in Tianjian year seven did Mao first ask that the great fur garment be made.

sentences.zh: 至是，有事於明堂，儀注猶云「服袞冕」。

translations.literal: At this time, when the Bright Hall rite was held, the protocol still read “wear the dragon robe.”
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall rite came due, the protocol still said, “Wear the dragon robe.”

sentences.zh: 懋駮云：「《禮》云『大裘而冕，祀昊天上帝亦如之。

translations.literal: Mao rebutted: “The Rites say, ‘Great fur garment and cap—sacrifice to the August Heaven above is also like this.’
translations.idiomatic: Mao objected: “The Rites say, ‘Great fur garment and cap—sacrifice to the August Heaven above is also like this.’

sentences.zh: 』良由天神尊遠，須貴誠質。

translations.literal: Truly because the spirits of Heaven are remote, one must honor sincerity and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s spirits are remote; one must honor sincerity and plainness.

sentences.zh: 今泛祭五帝，理不容文。

translations.literal: Now a general sacrifice to the Five Emperors cannot allow ornament.”
translations.idiomatic: A general sacrifice to the Five Emperors cannot permit ornament.”

sentences.zh: 」改服大裘，自此始也。

translations.literal: ” The change to the great fur garment began from this.
translations.idiomatic: ” The great fur garment began here.

sentences.zh: 又降敕問：「凡求陰陽，應各從其類，今雩祭燔柴，以火祈水，意以爲疑。

translations.literal: An edict also questioned: “In seeking yin and yang, each should follow its kind; now the Yu sacrifice burns firewood—using fire to pray for water—your servant finds this doubtful.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict also asked: “Seeking yin and yang should follow each kind; the Yu sacrifice burns firewood—fire to pray for water—your servant doubts this.”

sentences.zh: 」懋答曰：「雩祭燔柴，經無其文，良由先儒不思故也。

translations.literal: ” Mao replied: “Burning firewood at the Yu sacrifice has no text in the classics; truly the former scholars never thought it through.
translations.idiomatic: ” Mao answered: “Burning firewood at the Yu sacrifice has no classical text; the former scholars simply never thought it through.

sentences.zh: 按周宣《雲漢》之詩曰：『上下奠瘞，靡神不宗。

translations.literal: Your servant finds that in King Xuan’s ode “Vast Heaven” it says: “Above and below, set out the offerings and bury the victims;
translations.idiomatic: The ode “Vast Heaven” in King Xuan’s reign says, “Above and below, set out offerings and bury victims;

sentences.zh: 』毛注云：『上祭天，下祭地，奠其幣，瘞其物。

translations.literal: ” Mao’s commentary says: “Above, sacrifice to Heaven; below, sacrifice to Earth—set out the silks, bury the things.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Mao’s commentary: “Above, sacrifice to Heaven; below, sacrifice to Earth—set out silks, bury victims.”

sentences.zh: 』以此而言，爲旱而祭天地，並有瘞埋之文，不見有燔柴之說。

translations.literal: From this it follows that in drought one sacrifices to Heaven and Earth; both have texts of burial in the ground, and nowhere is burning firewood mentioned.
translations.idiomatic: So in drought one sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, with burial rites for both and no mention of burning firewood.

sentences.zh: 若以祭五帝必應燔柴者，今明常之禮，又無其事。

translations.literal: If sacrificing to the Five Emperors must burn firewood, then in the regular rites of the bright hall there is again no such affair.
translations.idiomatic: If the Five Emperors’ sacrifice must burn firewood, the regular Bright Hall rites have no such thing either.

sentences.zh: 且《禮》又云『埋少牢以祭時』，時之功是五帝，此又是不用柴之證矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rites also say, “Bury a young ox to sacrifice to the season”—the season’s achievement is the Five Emperors; this again is proof that firewood is not used.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites also say, “Bury a young ox to sacrifice to the season”—the season’s work is the Five Emperors’; again, no firewood.

sentences.zh: 昔雩壇在南方正陽位，有乖求神；

translations.literal: Formerly the Yu altar stood in the due-south position of the yang, at odds with seeking the spirits;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Yu altar stood due south in the yang position, ill-suited to seeking spirits;

sentences.zh: 而已移于東，實柴之禮猶未革。

translations.literal: though it was already moved eastward, the rite of burning firewood was still not reformed.
translations.idiomatic: though moved eastward, the firewood rite was still unreformed.

sentences.zh: 請停用柴，其牲牢等物，悉從坎瘞，以符周宣《雲漢》之說。

translations.literal: Your servant requests that burning firewood be discontinued; oxen and the like should all follow the pit burial, to accord with King Xuan’s “Vast Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks that firewood be discontinued and oxen and the rest buried in the pit, to match King Xuan’s “Vast Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 」詔並從之。

translations.literal: ” Edicts accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Edicts accepted everything.

sentences.zh: 凡諸禮儀，多所刊正。

translations.literal: In ritual matters of every kind he corrected many errors.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual matters of every kind he corrected much.

sentences.zh: 以足疾出爲始平太守，政有能名。

translations.literal: Because of foot ailment he went out as Grand Administrator of Shiping; his administration won a name for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Foot ailment sent him out as Grand Administrator of Shiping, where his rule won a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，轉天門太守。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Regular Cavalier Attendant and transferred to Grand Administrator of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: He was given Regular Cavalier Attendant and became Grand Administrator of Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，皇太子召諸儒參錄《長春義記》。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong the crown prince summoned the Confucians to compile the Record of the Meaning of the Everlasting Spring.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong year three the crown prince summoned Confucians to compile the Record of the Meaning of the Everlasting Spring.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜中庶子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In that year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 撰《述行記》四卷，有集十五卷。

translations.literal: He compiled A Record of Conduct in four scrolls and left a collected works in fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote A Record of Conduct in four scrolls and left collected works in fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：司馬褧儒術博通，到漑文義優敏，顯、懋、之遴強學浹洽，並職經便繁，應對左右，斯蓋嚴、朱之任焉。

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, said: Sima Jiong was broadly versed in Confucian learning; Dao Gai was quick and fine in literary meaning; Xian, Mao, and Zhilin were strong students, thorough and penetrating—all held posts heavy with the classics, answering at the ruler’s side; this was the charge of Yan and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Chen’s Minister of Personnel, said: Sima Jiong mastered Confucian learning; Dao Gai was quick and fine in letters; Xian, Mao, and Zhilin studied hard and knew their fields through— all served amid the classics at the ruler’s elbow, the office of Yan and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 而漑、之遴遂至顯貴，亟拾青紫；

translations.literal: Yet Gai and Zhilin rose to conspicuous wealth and repeatedly gathered the blue and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gai and Zhilin rose to great wealth and repeatedly took the blue and purple.

sentences.zh: 然非遇時，焉能致此仕也。

translations.literal: Had they not met the times, how could they have reached such posts?
translations.idiomatic: Without the times on their side, how could they have reached such posts?
